materials:
一、30秒速览（全部是铁证级事实）
- 1587年，约115名英格兰男女和儿童（含孕妇）在约翰·怀特率领下抵达今美国北卡罗来纳州罗阿诺克岛，原定目的地是切萨皮克湾，被领航员强行留在罗阿诺克岛。【一手文献】
- 1587年8月18日，弗吉尼亚·戴尔出生，是有文献记录的第一位出生在美洲的英格兰人后代。【一手文献】
- 1587年8月27日，总督怀特回英格兰求援，因西班牙无敌舰队战争被耽搁三年。
- 1590年8月18日怀特返回，殖民地空无一人，房屋被有序拆除，栅栏柱上刻着"CROATOAN"（克罗阿坦），树上刻着"CRO"，且没有事先约定的遇险信号（马耳他十字）。【一手文献】
- 这批人的最终命运，至今没有确证。
二、完整时间线（每条均标注来源）
背景与第一次探险（1584）
- 1584年3月25日：英格兰女王伊丽莎白一世向沃尔特·雷利爵士（Sir Walter Raleigh）颁发特许状，授权其在北美建立殖民地，条件是最迟1591年前建成，否则丧失殖民权。【一手文献：特许状原文存档】
- 1584年4月27日：菲利普·阿玛达斯（Philip Amadas）与亚瑟·巴洛（Arthur Barlowe）率两艘船从英格兰出发。
- 1584年7月13日：船队在今北卡罗来纳外滩群岛登陆，登陆点被命名为"费迪南多港"（Port Ferdinando）。这是英格兰旗帜首次在美洲升起。
- 探险队与当地的塞科坦人（Secotan）建立接触；时任酋长温吉纳（Wingina）因伤由其弟格兰加尼梅奥（Granganimeo）出面接待。
- 1584年秋：船队返回英格兰，带回两名原住民——克罗阿坦人曼特奥（Manteo，其母为克罗阿坦岛酋长）和塞科坦人万奇斯（Wanchese）。
- 1585年：伊丽莎白女王册封雷利为爵士，并将这片土地命名为"弗吉尼亚"（Virginia，意为"处女之地"，致敬未婚的女王）。
莱恩军事殖民地（1585–1586，非本次文案主角，但直接决定1587年定居者的处境）
- 1585年4月9日：理查德·格伦维尔爵士（Sir Richard Grenville）率七艘船、约600人从普利茅斯出发。随船有画家约翰·怀特、科学家托马斯·哈里奥特（Thomas Harriot）、冶金学家约阿希姆·甘斯（Joachim Gans，布拉格出生的犹太人，一般认为是有记录的第一位踏上美洲的犹太人）。【一手文献：哈克卢伊特《主要航海记》】
- 1585年6月26日：旗舰"老虎号"（Tiger）在奥克拉科克水道搁浅，大量补给损毁。
- 1585年7月11日：格伦维尔率60人考察大陆；因一只银杯失窃，阿玛达斯下令焚毁阿夸斯科戈克村（Aquascogoc）。此事是英人与原住民关系恶化的起点。【一手文献】
- 1585年8月25日：格伦维尔返英，留下拉尔夫·莱恩（Ralph Lane）率107人驻守罗阿诺克岛北端的土木堡垒。
- 1585年秋—1586年春：殖民者多次向原住民索取粮食；英国人带来的疾病导致原住民大量死亡；酋长温吉纳改名为佩米萨潘（Pemisapan，大意为"提防白人者"），并切断粮食供应。
- 1586年6月1日：莱恩率26人突袭大陆村庄达萨蒙奎皮克（Dasamongueponke），佩米萨潘被击毙（阿玛达斯开枪、爱德华·纽金特斩首）。【一手文献：莱恩本人的报告】
- 1586年6月8日：弗朗西斯·德雷克爵士（Sir Francis Drake）率23艘船抵达；一场持续三天的飓风吹散舰队。
- 1586年6月18–19日：莱恩殖民地全员随德雷克撤回英格兰（3人外出未归，被遗留在岛上，下落不明）。
- 1586年7月（数周内）：格伦维尔的补给舰队抵达，发现殖民地已空，留下15人驻守堡垒后返英。这15人后被原住民袭击，至少1人死亡，其余被赶离岛屿，最终命运无记录。
1587年"失落殖民地"（文案核心）
- 1587年1月7日：雷利批准成立"罗利城"（Cittie of Raleigh）公司，任命约翰·怀特为总督，配12名助理。计划定居点是切萨皮克湾，不是罗阿诺克岛。
- 1587年5月8日：三艘船（旗舰"雄狮号"Lion、一艘轻快帆船、一艘全帆装小艇）载约115名定居者从普利茅斯出发。定居者多为伦敦中产市民，这次是首次带妇女儿童的定居尝试（此前1585年纯属军事据点）。【一手文献：怀特航海日志】
- 1587年7月22日：船队抵达外滩群岛。怀特本欲带40人上岛与格伦维尔留下的15人会合后再去切萨皮克湾，但领航员西蒙·费尔南德斯（Simon Fernandes，葡萄牙裔）命令水手将定居者全部卸在罗阿诺克岛，拒绝继续北上。这是整个悲剧的关键转折点。【一手文献：怀特航海日志】
- 1587年7月22–23日：登岛后只发现一具人类遗骨（怀特判断为15名留守者之一）；莱恩堡垒已被拆毁，房屋空置，爬满瓜藤，有鹿在屋内进食。【一手文献：怀特航海日志】
- 1587年7月25日：第三艘船到达，全员上岸，开始修复旧屋、搭建新居。
- 1587年7月28日：总督助理乔治·豪（George Howe）独自在阿尔伯马尔湾捕蟹时被杀，尸体中16支箭并遭击打。【一手文献】
- 1587年7月31日：定居者在曼特奥帮助下与克罗阿坦人（Croatoan，居今哈特拉斯岛，态度友好）会面，得知15名留守者与乔治·豪均死于以万奇斯为首的大陆部落联盟之手。
- 1587年8月8日或9日（不同文献相差一天）：怀特率24人报复性突袭达萨蒙奎皮克村，但敌对部落已逃走，误杀了进村捡拾粮食的友好克罗阿坦人。曼特奥出面调解，克罗阿坦人原谅了定居者。【一手文献：怀特航海日志】
- 1587年8月13日：曼特奥按英格兰国教仪式受洗，获封"罗阿诺克与达萨蒙奎皮克领主"。这被北美官方史料认定为北美最早的新教洗礼仪式之一。【一手文献】
- 1587年8月18日：怀特之女埃莉诺·戴尔（Eleanor Dare，丈夫为阿纳尼亚斯·戴尔 Ananias Dare）产下一女，取名弗吉尼亚·戴尔（Virginia Dare）——有记录的第一位出生在美洲的英格兰人后代，并于随后数日内的周日受洗。不久后另一名定居者玛格丽·哈维（Margery Harvie）也产下一子，史称"哈维家的婴儿"，除此之外无任何记载。【一手文献：怀特航海日志】
- 同期，定居者已决定从罗阿诺克岛向内陆迁移约50英里（约80公里）。【一手文献：怀特航海日志原话"they were prepared to remove from Roanoak 50 miles into the maine"】
- 1587年8月27日：在定居者集体恳求下，怀特启程回英格兰筹运补给。临行前双方约定：若迁移，须在树上或门柱刻下目的地名称；若被迫离开（遇险），须在刻字上方加刻马耳他十字。【一手文献：怀特航海日志】
- 1587年11月5日：怀特回到英格兰。
被战争耽误的三年（1588–1590）
- 1588年：西班牙无敌舰队压境，伊丽莎白女王禁止一切可用船只离港。
- 1588年4月22日：怀特获准带两艘小船（"勇敢号"Brave、"雌鹿号"Roe）出发，但船长沿途企图劫掠西班牙船只牟利；5月6日在摩洛哥近海遭法国海盗袭击，近24名船员死亡，补给被劫，被迫返航。【一手文献】
- 1588年：西班牙国王腓力二世派比森特·冈萨雷斯（Vicente González）搜索切萨皮克湾；一无所获，返程时偶然发现费迪南多港，记录该港"已被废弃"。【西班牙官方档案，属第三方旁证】
1590年：发现空城（全文最重要的原始记录）
- 1590年3月：怀特搭约翰·沃茨组织的私掠船队出发，旗舰"希望号"（Hopewell）与"月光号"（Moonlight）负责送他到罗阿诺克。
- 1590年8月15–17日：船队在外滩群岛外多次看到岛上升起烟柱与火光；登陆过程遭遇恶劣海况，7名水手溺亡。
- 1590年8月18日（弗吉尼亚·戴尔3岁生日当天）：怀特登上罗阿诺克岛。怀特本人在航海日志中记录的发现如下【一手文献，1600年由哈克卢伊特出版，原文存于《主要航海记》第三卷】：
  a. 岸边一棵树的高处刻着三个罗马字母"CRO"；
  b. 营地房屋被拆除（不是焚毁、不是毁坏的痕迹），场地四周新立起高大的木栅栏，"带有幕墙和侧堡，俨然一座堡垒"；
  c. 入口右侧一根主柱剥去树皮，离地5英尺处"以工整的大写字母刻着 CROATOAN（克罗阿坦），没有十字或任何遇险标记"；
  d. 栅栏内散落铁条、两块铅锭、四支铁枪、铁炮弹等重物，已被荒草覆盖；
  e. 殖民地的船只和小炮均不见踪影；
  f. 定居者事先掩埋的多只箱子被掘出撬开，其中三只是怀特本人的——书籍被撕毁、画作与地图的框架被雨水泡烂、铠甲锈蚀。怀特判断系达萨蒙奎皮克的敌对部落所为。
- 怀特据此判断定居者按计划安全迁往克罗阿坦岛（曼特奥的家乡，今哈特拉斯岛）。次日拟前往克罗阿坦岛搜救，但"希望号"锚链崩断、风暴逼近，被迫放弃。
- 1590年10月24日：怀特回到普利茅斯。此后再未踏上美洲。1593年他从爱尔兰致信出版商后，史料中再无其确切生平记录。
- 怀特1593年致哈克卢伊特的信中写道，只能把殖民者及其家人的命运"交托给全能者的仁慈庇佑"。【一手文献】
失踪后的搜寻（1594–1603）
- 1594年：有人请愿宣告阿纳尼亚斯·戴尔法律死亡，以便其在英格兰的儿子继承遗产；1597年获批。这是英格兰官方对定居者"推定死亡"的唯一法律记录。【后世记录：英格兰法律文书】
- 1595年：雷利远航自称寻找殖民者，后承认是寻找"黄金国"（El Dorado）的掩护说辞。【后世记录】
- 1602年：雷利出资派塞缪尔·梅斯（Samuel Mace）赴外滩群岛搜寻，但船队优先在克罗阿坦岛以南采收当时价格暴涨的檫木（sassafras），接近哈特拉斯时因天气恶劣返航，没有实际展开搜寻。【后世记录】
- 1603年7月29日：巴塞洛缪·吉尔伯特（Bartholomew Gilbert）率最后一次搜寻队前往切萨皮克湾方向，登陆队包括吉尔伯特本人全部被原住民杀死，余众空手返航。【后世记录】
- 1603年：雷利卷入"主谋阴谋案"（Main Plot）被捕，其对弗吉尼亚的特许权实际终结。

四、定居者人数与名单（数字争议要说清楚）
这一点写文案时最容易出错，务必按以下口径表述：
- 哈克卢伊特1600年出版的名单共列 119个名字，但该名单包含怀特本人、领航员费尔南德斯（两人都返回了英格兰）、以及出发后死亡的两人，还有一个名字重复出现。【一手文献，但有瑕疵】
- 史学界权威大卫·比尔斯·奎因（David Beers Quinn，1955年考证）核定：怀特1587年8月离开时，实际留在岛上的约为114人，含两名在岛上出生的婴儿和曼特奥、托瓦伊（Towaye）两名原住民。
- 美国国家公园管理局（NPS）官方展陈通行口径为 117人（出发时的定居者口径）。
- 保守统计为112人，最高估计121人。
文案建议表述："约115名定居者（官方名单119个名字，扣除随船返回者与病故者，史学界核定实际留岛约114人）"。
名单可查性：119人完整名单存于哈克卢伊特《主要航海记》，其中女性17人，儿童9–11人（各文献口径不一）。知名者包括：戴尔一家、哈维夫妇、乔治·豪等。需要完整名单可另行提取。
五、失踪后的第三方记录（詹姆斯敦时期，均属"据记载/声称"级别）
以下均为事件发生约20年后的二手记录，来自詹姆斯敦殖民者听闻的原住民口述，没有任何实物证据佐证，引用时必须加限定词。
- 1607–1608年：詹姆斯敦的约翰·史密斯（John Smith）从波瓦坦人处听说，有"穿着欧洲服装的人"住在奥卡纳霍南（Ocanahonan）等地；并据此派人搜寻，一无所获。【后世记录：史密斯《真实关系》】
- 1608年"苏尼加地图"（Zúñiga Map）：詹姆斯敦定居者弗朗西斯·纳尔逊绘制的草图被西班牙驻英大使佩德罗·德·苏尼加获得并呈交西班牙国王（1890年在西班牙档案中重新发现）。图上标注：在帕克勒卡尼克（Pakrakanick）"有四名穿衣着的男子，来自罗阿诺克"。【后世记录：实物地图存世，但内容属传闻记录】
- 1610年：弗吉尼亚公司官方文件《真实而诚挚的宣告》称，搜寻者虽未能与幸存者交谈，但"发现了刻在树皮上的十字与字母——基督徒新刻的确凿标记"。【后世记录：官方出版物】
- 1612年：詹姆斯敦殖民地秘书威廉·斯特雷奇（William Strachey）在《弗吉尼亚不列颠旅行史》中写道：
  a. 佩卡雷卡尼克（Peccarecanick）与奥查纳霍恩（Ochanahoen）两地的原住民会造"石墙两层楼房"，据说是从罗阿诺克逃出的英格兰人教的；
  b. 波瓦坦酋长瓦洪塞纳卡（Wahunsenacawh，即俗称的"波瓦坦酋长"，宝嘉康蒂之父）下令屠杀时，有7人逃脱——4名男子、2个男孩、1名少女，逃至伊阿诺科（Eyanoco）酋长庇护下的里塔诺克（Ritanoc）；
  c. 波瓦坦一方声称屠杀发生于詹姆斯敦建立前不久，并展示过若干英格兰铁器作为凭证。

八、至今无法证实的问题（写文案只能这么表述）
1. 定居者离开罗阿诺克岛后具体去了哪里、走了哪条路线——无确证。
2. 他们是否全部抵达克罗阿坦（哈特拉斯岛）——无确证，只有刻字指向和间接实物。
3. 是否有部分人迁往内陆（X遗址方向）或北上切萨皮克湾——各有间接线索，均无确证。
4. 是否有人被波瓦坦人杀死——只有约20年后的传闻记录，无实物、无遗骸。

原片FS08「元设定溶解+限时潜入」是向配角坦白穿越者身份、换装潜入头等舱。本题可用「1587年7月31日与克罗阿坦人会面、曼特奥调停、得知15名留守者死讯」承担meta_twist高峰（PK03 75分）——把「向戏中角色揭示镜头外真相」改为「曼特奥as cultural broker揭示两个世界的miscommunication」，把「换装潜入」改为「在曼特奥陪同下短暂进入原住民村落」，功能equivalent：both是跨越forbidden boundary、both有insider帮助、both制造「两个世界短暂接触」的high-stakes moment

facts.content: 1587年7月22日，约115名英格兰定居者（含17名女性、9-11名儿童）抵达今美国北卡罗来纳州罗阿诺克岛
facts.source: 约翰·怀特航海日志，收录于哈克卢伊特《主要航海记》第三卷
facts.region: 北卡罗来纳州罗阿诺克岛

facts.content: 怀特本欲带40人上岛与留守者会合后再去切萨皮克湾（原定目的地），但领航员西蒙·费尔南德斯命令水手将定居者全部卸在罗阿诺克岛，拒绝继续北上
facts.source: 约翰·怀特航海日志

facts.content: 登岛后只发现一具人类遗骨（怀特判断为15名留守者之一），莱恩堡垒已被拆毁，房屋空置，爬满瓜藤，有鹿在屋内进食
facts.source: 约翰·怀特航海日志

facts.content: 1587年定居者多为伦敦中产市民，参与「罗利城公司」需自备工具、种子和部分补给，类比1585年莱恩殖民地的三等舱船票约为当时工匠年收入的1/4
facts.source: 参考1585-1587年英格兰工匠年收入约10-15英镑（《剑桥英国经济史》）与跨大西洋航程成本（哈克卢伊特记录）

facts.content: 1587年7月28日，总督助理乔治·豪独自在阿尔伯马尔湾（Albemarle Sound）捕蟹时被杀，尸体中16支箭并遭击打
facts.source: 约翰·怀特航海日志

facts.content: 1587年7月31日，定居者在曼特奥帮助下与克罗阿坦人会面，得知15名留守者与乔治·豪均死于以万奇斯为首的大陆部落联盟之手
facts.source: 约翰·怀特航海日志
facts.region: 罗阿诺克岛-克罗阿坦岛之间

facts.content: 1587年8月8日或9日，怀特率24人报复性突袭达萨蒙奎皮克村（Dasamongueponke），但敌对部落已逃走，误杀了进村捡拾粮食的友好克罗阿坦人；曼特奥出面调解，克罗阿坦人原谅了定居者
facts.source: 约翰·怀特航海日志
facts.region: 达萨蒙奎皮克村（今北卡大陆）

facts.content: 1587年8月13日，曼特奥按英格兰国教仪式受洗，获封「罗阿诺克与达萨蒙奎皮克领主」，这是北美最早的新教洗礼仪式之一
facts.source: 约翰·怀特航海日志；美国国家公园管理局官方记录

facts.slot: 第一个美洲英格兰婴儿
facts.content: 1587年8月18日，怀特之女埃莉诺·戴尔产下一女，取名弗吉尼亚·戴尔（Virginia Dare），是有文献记录的第一位出生在美洲的英格兰人后代，并于随后数日内的周日受洗
facts.source: 约翰·怀特航海日志

facts.content: 1587年8月中下旬（弗吉尼亚出生后、怀特离开前），定居者已决定从罗阿诺克岛向内陆迁移约50英里（约80公里）
facts.source: 约翰·怀特航海日志原话「they were prepared to remove from Roanoak 50 miles into the maine」

facts.content: 1587-1589年是罗阿诺克地区800年来最干旱的三年；1587年夏（定居者登岛时）是800年来最差的生长季
facts.source: 阿肯色大学David Stahle与威廉与玛丽学院Dennis Blanton，树轮重建降水数据，发表于《科学》期刊1998年
facts.region: 北卡罗来纳州罗阿诺克岛周边

facts.slot: 定居者集体恳求怀特回英
facts.content: 1587年8月27日启程前，定居者集体恳求怀特回英格兰筹运补给（怀特本人不愿离开女儿和外孙女，但在众人insistence下同意）
facts.source: 约翰·怀特航海日志

facts.content: 1587年8月27日临行前，怀特与定居者约定：若迁移，须在树上或门柱刻下目的地名称；若被迫离开（遇险），须在刻字上方加刻马耳他十字
facts.source: 约翰·怀特航海日志

facts.content: 1587年8月27日，怀特启程回英格兰；1587年11月5日抵达英格兰
facts.source: 约翰·怀特航海日志

facts.content: 1588年西班牙无敌舰队压境，伊丽莎白女王禁止一切可用船只离港；怀特1588年4月22日带两艘小船出发，5月6日遭法国海盗袭击、近24名船员死亡、补给被劫，被迫返航
facts.source: 约翰·怀特航海日志；哈克卢伊特《主要航海记》

facts.content: 1590年8月15-17日，怀特搭乘的船队在外滩群岛外多次看到岛上升起烟柱与火光；登陆过程遭遇恶劣海况，7名水手溺亡
facts.source: 约翰·怀特航海日志，收录于哈克卢伊特《主要航海记》第三卷

facts.content: 1590年8月18日（弗吉尼亚·戴尔3岁生日当天），怀特登上罗阿诺克岛，发现：(1)岸边树高处刻着「CRO」(2)营地房屋被有序拆除、场地四周新立高大木栅栏「带有幕墙和侧堡，俨然一座堡垒」(3)入口右侧主柱离地5英尺处「以工整的大写字母刻着CROATOAN，没有十字或任何遇险标记」(4)栅栏内散落铁条、铅锭、铁枪、炮弹等重物，已被荒草覆盖(5)定居者的船只和小炮均不见踪影(6)怀特本人掩埋的箱子被掘出撬开，书籍撕毁、画作地图泡烂、铠甲锈蚀
facts.source: 约翰·怀特航海日志，1600年由哈克卢伊特出版

facts.content: 怀特据此判断定居者按计划安全迁往克罗阿坦岛（曼特奥的家乡，今哈特拉斯岛）；次日拟前往搜救，但「希望号」锚链崩断、风暴逼近，被迫放弃
facts.source: 约翰·怀特航海日志

facts.content: 1593年，怀特从爱尔兰致信出版商哈克卢伊特，写道只能把殖民者及其家人的命运「交托给全能者的仁慈庇佑」（commit them to the merciful providence of the Almighty）；此后史料中再无其确切生平记录
facts.source: 怀特1593年致哈克卢伊特信件，收录于《主要航海记》

facts.content: 哈克卢伊特1600年出版的名单共列119个名字，但包含怀特本人、领航员费尔南德斯（两人都返回了英格兰）、以及出发后死亡的两人，还有一个名字重复；史学界权威David Beers Quinn 1955年核定：怀特1587年8月离开时，实际留在岛上的约为114人，含两名在岛上出生的婴儿和曼特奥、托瓦伊两名原住民
facts.source: David Beers Quinn《The Roanoke Voyages 1584-1590》1955年考证；美国国家公园管理局官方展陈通行口径为117人

facts.content: 四百多年来，从未发现过任何一具可确认为1587年定居者的墓葬或遗骸，也未发现任何一件能确指到名单上某个具体人物的随身物品
facts.source: 美国国家公园管理局雷利堡国家历史遗址官方声明；First Colony Foundation考古总结

facts.slot: 考古发现：哈特拉斯岛锤鳞
facts.content: 2025年5月，布里斯托大学Mark Horton与克罗阿坦考古学会在哈特拉斯岛贝壳堆下层（初步断代为16世纪末）发现两堆锤鳞（hammerscale，铁匠锻铁时崩落的氧化铁屑）；主张：锤鳞不会被交易，而当地原住民不掌握锻铁技术，故指向英格兰人曾在岛上打铁；但该成果尚未经同行评审，质疑者指出未发现配套锻炉
facts.source: Mark Horton与Scott Dawson 2025年5月发布（via新闻报道）；北卡大学历史学家Kathleen DuVal评论
facts.region: 哈特拉斯岛（原克罗阿坦岛）

candidates.text: July 22nd, 1587. I'm standing on Roanoke Island with 115 English settlers—families, kids, two pregnant women. We were supposed to go to Chesapeake Bay. But the pilot just dumped us here and sailed away. And I know what's going to happen: in three years, when the ships come back, we'll all be gone. Every single one of us. No bodies. No graves. Just one word carved on a post: CROATOAN. Let me show you how it happened.

August 18th, 1587. My granddaughter Virginia was just born—first English baby born in America. In three years, she'll vanish. Her mother, my daughter Eleanor, will vanish. All 115 of us will vanish. And 437 years later, no one will ever find a single body. I'm about to live through the most famous disappearance in American history. And I'm going to tell you exactly what it felt like to be left behind.

1587. I'm a colonist on Roanoke Island, and the ships just left us here—wrong place, wrong supplies, surrounded by people who already killed 15 Englishmen. In nine days, my granddaughter will be born. In five weeks, I'll have to sail back to England for help. And I'll never see any of them again. This is the Lost Colony. But I'm going to show you: we weren't lost. We were abandoned.

July 22nd, 1587. I'm standing on Roanoke Island. 115 English settlers around me. We were supposed to go to Chesapeake Bay. That was the plan. But the pilot refused. He forced us off here. Wrong island. Wrong supplies. And there are people here who've already killed Englishmen. I'm going to try to get inland. I need to warn them.

[CH02 | 0:22-0:39 | authenticity_contract]

Everything you're seeing comes from John White's watercolors. He painted 75 images between 1585 and 1587. They're in the British Museum now. We've colorized them and animated them. This is as close as we can get to what it actually looked like. No exaggeration.

[CH03 | 0:39-0:54 | mission_briefing]

Let me tell you what I'm going to do. First: explore this island. See what's left of the old fort. Meet the people I'll be living with. Second: I need to find a way to convince them we have to leave. Move inland. Because I know what's coming.

[CH04 | 0:54-1:25 | threshold_crossing]

Okay, so we're walking into the settlement now. The old fort Lane built—it's torn down. Just scattered timbers. The houses are empty. Vines growing through the windows. I can see a deer inside one of them, eating grass. It's humid here. Really humid. The wood smells like rot. This is not where we were supposed to be. We were supposed to have a proper fort. Fresh water. Good land. This is just… remnants.

[CH05 | 1:25-2:47 | daily_life_exploration]

All right, so we've been here about a week now. We're fixing up these old houses. Mine has four walls. Actual walls. The roof leaks but we patched it with bark. There's a wooden platform for sleeping. No mattress. Just boards. I've slept on worse. The sheets are clean, though. We brought those from England. There's no running water inside. We haul it from a creek about 200 feet away. It's drinkable. Barely. The heat is constant. It's like walking through soup. Mosquitoes everywhere. I have bites on my arms, my neck, my ankles. The wood is always damp. Our clothes don't dry properly. They just hang there, heavy and moist. But honestly, I've stayed in worse boarding houses in London. At least here we don't share beds. The latrines are communal pits outside the palisade. Not pleasant. But functional. Every morning we wake up, haul water, repair something that broke overnight. The work is endless. But we're settling in.

[CH06 | 2:47-4:43 | steerage_social_life]

Let me introduce you to some people. This is Eleanor. She's my daughter. Eight months pregnant. Her husband Ananias is building a crib out of driftwood. He's out there every day, sanding it smooth so the baby won't get splinters. This is George Howe. He's one of the assistants. Every morning he goes down to the sound to catch crabs. He says they're bigger here than in England. He's right. We eat a lot of crab. This is Margery Harvie. Also pregnant. Due any day now. She and Eleanor sit together in the shade, sewing baby clothes. And this is Manteo. He's Croatoan. He's been helping us communicate with the local tribes. Teaching us which plants are safe to eat. The food here is different. Corn. Beans. Squash. The Croatoans showed us how to grow them. It's not bad. Honestly, it's better than what we had on the ship. But I miss bread. Real English bread. We don't have wheat here. We make a kind of flat cake from cornmeal. It's edible. Eleanor says once the baby comes, we'll have a feast. Manteo promised to bring fish. George will bring crabs. We'll all sit together and celebrate the first English child born in Virginia. That's what we're calling this place. Virginia. After the Queen.

[CH07 | 4:43-5:59 | communal_celebration]

August 18th, 1587. Eleanor's baby was born this morning. A girl. She named her Virginia Dare. First English child born here. I held her. She's so small. Her fingers are tiny. She has Eleanor's eyes. We spent the afternoon preparing for the baptism. I washed the swaddling cloths. There was blood on them. But they're the only cloths we have. Manteo brought gifts from his people. Corn. Fish. Woven baskets. We gathered around the baby and sang hymns. I don't know all the words. But nobody cared. Five days later, August 13th, we held another ceremony. Manteo was baptized. Christened in the Church of England. Raleigh named him Lord of Roanoke and Dasamongueponke. First Native convert. We thought this meant peace. We thought we were building something together. A community. I felt like I belonged here. Like we all did.

[CH08 | 5:59-7:10 | confession_and_heist]

A few days after the baptism, Manteo pulled me aside. He said, You need to understand what happened here. He took me to meet his people. The Croatoans. They told me the truth. The 15 Englishmen Lane left behind—they're dead. All of them. Killed by Wanchese and his alliance. Mainland tribes. And George Howe, the man who went crabbing every morning. They found his body in the sound. Sixteen arrows in him. His skull crushed. Manteo handed me an English sword. One of the men who died. He said, You're not safe here. You need to leave. I asked him, Can we come with you? To Croatoan? He said, Maybe. But not now. You need to be very careful. So we decided. We'll move inland. Away from Wanchese. Closer to Manteo's people. Somewhere safer.

[CH09 | 7:10-8:24 | forbidden_luxury_reveal]

August 8th, 1587. John White organized a raid. Retaliation for George Howe's death. Twenty-four men. I went with them. We marched through dense forest into mainland territory. Dasamongueponke village. It took hours. The heat was brutal. When we arrived, the village was empty. But I could see their longhouses. Bark-covered. About 80 feet long. Cooking pits still warm. Corn drying on racks. This is where they killed George. This is where they killed the 15 men. Then we heard voices. We thought it was Wanchese's people. We opened fire. But it wasn't Wanchese. It was Croatoans. Manteo's people. Gathering leftover corn from the abandoned village. Manteo ran out shouting, Stop! These are my people! We came here to punish murderers. And we just shot our only friends. The Croatoans forgave us. But the damage was done.

[CH10 | 8:24-9:18 | luxury_catalog]

August 13th. Manteo's baptism. He kneels. The minister pours water over his head. Raleigh's representative proclaims him Lord of Roanoke. We thought this meant alliance. Protection. August 18th. Virginia's birth. I hold her again that night. She's nine days old now. We sit around the fire, talking about where we'll build houses inland. Fifty miles into the mainland. Fresh water. Better land. Away from the coast. Away from Wanchese. The stars are out over the sound. It's beautiful. Quiet. Then Eleanor asks me: Father, when will you go back to England for supplies? I freeze. I'd been avoiding this. But she's right. We need more people. More tools. More food. I realize: I have to leave them. I have to leave my daughter and my nine-day-old granddaughter and sail back to England. And I don't know when I'll see them again.

[CH11 | 9:18-9:54 | dramatic_irony_turn]

August 27th, 1587. The colonists gathered around me. All of them. Begging. You have to go back, John. We need supplies. We need reinforcements. I looked at Eleanor holding Virginia. I said, I don't want to leave you. She said, Father, you have to. So we made a plan. If they move while I'm gone, they'll carve the name of the place on a tree. If they're in distress—forced to leave under attack—they'll carve a Maltese cross above the name. I memorized it. Tree. Name. Cross if danger.

[CH12 | 9:54-10:41 | plan_rehearsal]

They told me the details. We'll move fifty miles inland. Into the mainland. Away from Wanchese. Closer to fresh water. I rehearsed what I'd tell the investors in London. The colonists are well. They've moved inland. You can find them at—but I didn't know where they'd be. I only knew they'd carve the name. I packed my things. My daughter's letters. My maps. My sketches. The chest was heavy. I practiced the words again. I'll be back by spring. That's what I'd say. Spring 1588. Six months. I can do that.

[CH13 | 10:41-11:23 | futile_warning]

August 27th, 1587. I boarded the ship. Eleanor stood on the shore, holding Virginia. Ananias had his arm around her. I waved goodbye. I shouted, I'll be back by spring! She shouted back, We'll be inland! Look for the carving! The ship started moving. I watched them get smaller. Dots on the beach. I told myself, I'll see them again. Six months. That's all. Of course I believed it. I don't blame myself for leaving. They insisted. They needed supplies. I was the only one who could get them. The sky was gray. The drought had been terrible all summer. I didn't know this was the last time I'd ever see my daughter.

[CH14 | 11:23-12:20 | countdown_and_impact]

I tried to return in 1588. But England was at war with Spain. The Armada. Queen Elizabeth forbade all ships from leaving port. April 22nd, 1588. I finally got two small ships. We sailed. May 6th. French pirates attacked us off the coast of Morocco. Twenty-four men died. We lost all the supplies. We had to turn back. I tried again. And again. Three years. August 15th, 1590. I finally returned. We saw smoke rising from the island. I thought, They're still there. They're alive. August 18th, 1590. Virginia's third birthday. I landed. The houses were gone. In their place: a tall wooden palisade. Like a fort. Curtain walls. Flankers. Inside, the ground was overgrown with grass. Scattered iron bars. Lead ingots. Rusted armor. Cannonballs. Their boats were gone. The small cannon, gone. On the right-hand post at the entrance, five feet up, carved in neat capital letters: CROATOAN. No cross. No distress mark. I also found my own chests. Broken open. My books torn apart. My maps soaked and ruined. My sketches destroyed. But no cross. That meant they left safely. They went to Croatoan. Manteo's island. They're there. They have to be there.

[CH15 | 12:20-13:16 | collapse_witnessing]

The captain said, We'll sail to Croatoan tomorrow. Find them. But that night, a storm hit. The anchor cable snapped. The ship was in danger. He had a choice: risk the ship and a hundred men to search for 114 colonists, or sail home. He chose to sail home. I begged him. Please. My daughter is there. My granddaughter is there. He said, We've done what we can. We tried. I couldn't argue with him. The storm was real. The risk was real. But I also couldn't look at that island anymore. Somewhere—inland, or on Croatoan—my daughter was waiting for me. Hoping I'd come back. And I was leaving her again. We sailed away. I never returned.

[CH16 | 13:16-14:00 | closure_reflection]

1593. I wrote to Richard Hakluyt from Ireland. I said I could only commit the colonists to the merciful providence of the Almighty. That's the last record of me. It's one thing to read that CROATOAN is a mystery. But it's another thing to stand in front of that post and know your daughter carved it. Know she and Ananias stood there with chisels, carving the name of the place they were going, hoping you'd understand. They weren't lost. They knew where they were going. I was the one who couldn't reach them.

[CH01 | 0:00-0:22 | immersive_premise_hook]

July 22nd, 1587. I'm standing on Roanoke Island. More than a hundred English settlers around me. We were supposed to go to Chesapeake Bay. That was the plan. But the pilot refused. He forced us off here. Wrong island. Wrong supplies. And there are people here who've already killed Englishmen. I'm going to try to get inland. I need to warn them.

[CH02 | 0:22-0:39 | authenticity_contract]

Everything you're seeing comes from John White's watercolors. He painted 75 images between 1585 and 1587. They're in the British Museum now. We've colorized them and animated them. This is the closest we'll ever get to seeing it as it was. No exaggeration.

[CH03 | 0:39-0:54 | mission_briefing]

Here's what I'm going to do. First: explore this island. See what's left of the old fort. Meet the people I'll be living with. Second: I need to find a way to convince them. We have to leave. Move inland. Because I know what's coming.

[CH04 | 0:54-1:25 | threshold_crossing]

Okay, so we're walking into the settlement now. The old fort Lane built—it's torn down. Just scattered timbers. The houses are empty. Vines growing through the windows. I can see a deer inside one of them, eating grass. It's humid here. Really humid. The wood smells like rot. This is not where we were supposed to be. We were supposed to have a proper fort. Fresh water. Good land. This is just… remnants.

[CH05 | 1:25-2:47 | daily_life_exploration]

All right, so we've been here about a week now. We're fixing up these old houses. Mine has four walls. Actual walls. The roof leaks but we patched it with bark. There's a wooden platform for sleeping. No mattress. Just boards. I've slept on worse. The sheets are clean, though. We brought those from England. There's no running water inside. We haul it from a creek about 200 feet away. It's drinkable. Barely. The heat is constant. It's like walking through soup. Mosquitoes everywhere. I have bites on my arms, my neck, my ankles. The wood is always damp. Our clothes don't dry properly. They just hang there, heavy and moist. But honestly, I've stayed in worse boarding houses in London. At least here we don't share beds. We dig latrines outside—communal pits, like any camp. Not pleasant. But functional. Every morning we wake up, haul water, repair something that broke overnight. The work is endless. But we're settling in.

[CH06 | 2:47-4:43 | steerage_social_life]

Let me introduce you to some people. This is Eleanor. She's my daughter. Eight months pregnant. Her husband Ananias is building a crib out of driftwood. He's out there every day, sanding it smooth so the baby won't get splinters. This is George Howe. He's one of the assistants. Every morning he goes down to the sound to catch crabs. He says they're bigger here than in England. He's right. We eat a lot of crab. This is Margery Harvie. Also pregnant. Due any day now. She and Eleanor sit together in the shade, sewing baby clothes. And this is Manteo. He's Croatoan. He's been helping us communicate with the local tribes. Teaching us which plants are safe to eat. The Croatoans teach us their foods: corn, beans, squash. We try to make a flat bread from cornmeal—it's not like home, but it's edible. Eleanor says once the baby comes, we'll have a feast. Manteo promised to bring fish. George will bring crabs. We'll all sit together and celebrate the first English child born in Virginia. That's what we're calling this place. Virginia. After the Queen.

[CH07 | 4:43-5:59 | communal_celebration]

August 18th, 1587. Eleanor's baby was born this morning. A girl. She named her Virginia Dare. First English child born here. I held her. She's so small. Her fingers are tiny. She has Eleanor's eyes. We spent the afternoon preparing for the baptism. I washed the swaddling cloths. There was blood on them. But they're the only cloths we have. Manteo brought gifts from his people. Corn. Fish. Woven baskets. We gathered around the baby and sang hymns. I don't know all the words. But nobody cared. Five days earlier, on August 13th, we held another ceremony. Manteo was baptized. Christened in the Church of England. Raleigh named him Lord of Roanoke and Dasamongueponke. First Native convert. We thought this meant peace. We thought we were building something together. A community. I felt like I belonged here. Like we all did.

[CH08 | 5:59-7:10 | confession_and_heist]

A few days after the baptism, Manteo pulled me aside. He said, You need to understand what happened here. He took me to meet his people. The Croatoans. They told me the truth. The 15 Englishmen Lane left behind—they're dead. All of them. Killed by Wanchese and his alliance. Mainland tribes. And George Howe, the man who went crabbing every morning. They found his body in the sound. Sixteen arrows in him. His skull crushed. Manteo handed me an English sword. One of the men who died. He said, You're not safe here. You need to leave. I asked him, Can we come with you? To Croatoan? He said, Maybe. But not now. You need to be very careful. So we decided. We'll move inland. Away from Wanchese. Closer to Manteo's people. Somewhere safer.

[CH09 | 7:10-8:24 | forbidden_luxury_reveal]

August 8th, 1587. John White organized a raid. Retaliation for George Howe's death. Twenty-four men. I went with them. We marched through dense forest into mainland territory. Dasamongueponke village. It took hours. The heat was brutal. When we arrived, the village was empty. But I could see their longhouses. Bark-covered. About 80 feet long. Cooking pits still warm. Corn drying on racks. This is where they killed George. This is where they killed the 15 men. Then we heard voices. We thought it was Wanchese's people. We opened fire. But it wasn't Wanchese. It was Croatoans. Manteo's people. Gathering leftover corn from the abandoned village. Manteo ran out shouting, Stop! These are my people! We came here to punish murderers. And we just shot our only friends. The Croatoans forgave us. But the damage was done.

[CH10 | 8:24-9:18 | luxury_catalog]

August 13th. Manteo's baptism. He kneels. The minister pours water over his head. Raleigh's representative proclaims him Lord of Roanoke. We thought this meant alliance. Protection. August 18th. Virginia's birth. I hold her again that night. She's nine days old now. We sit around the fire, talking about where we'll build houses inland. Fifty miles into the mainland. Fresh water. Better land. Away from the coast. Away from Wanchese. The stars are out over the sound. It's beautiful. Quiet. Then Eleanor asks me: Father, when will you go back to England for supplies? I freeze. I'd been avoiding this. But she's right. We need more people. More tools. More food. I realize: I have to leave them. I have to leave my daughter and my nine-day-old granddaughter and sail back to England. And I don't know when I'll see them again.

[CH11 | 9:18-9:54 | dramatic_irony_turn]

August 27th, 1587. The colonists gathered around me. All of them. Begging. You have to go back, John. We need supplies. We need reinforcements. I looked at Eleanor holding Virginia. I said, I don't want to leave you. She said, Father, you have to. So we made a plan. If they move while I'm gone, they'll carve the name of the place on a tree. If they're in distress—forced to leave under attack—they'll carve a Maltese cross above the name. I memorized it. Tree. Name. Cross if danger.

[CH12 | 9:54-10:41 | plan_rehearsal]

They told me the details. We'll move fifty miles inland. Into the mainland. Away from Wanchese. Closer to fresh water. I rehearsed what I'd tell the investors in London. The colonists are well. They've moved inland. You can find them at—but I didn't know where they'd be. I only knew they'd carve the name. I packed my things. My daughter's letters. My maps. My sketches. The chest was heavy. I practiced the words again. I'll be back by spring. That's what I'd say. Spring 1588. Six months. I can do that.

[CH13 | 10:41-11:23 | futile_warning]

August 27th, 1587. I boarded the ship. Eleanor stood on the shore, holding Virginia. Ananias had his arm around her. I waved goodbye. I shouted, I'll be back by spring! She shouted back, We'll be inland! Look for the carving! The ship started moving. I watched them get smaller. Dots on the beach. I told myself, I'll see them again. Six months. That's all. Of course I believed it. I don't blame myself for leaving. They insisted. They needed supplies. I was the only one who could get them. The sky was gray. The drought had been terrible all summer. I didn't know this was the last time I'd ever see my daughter.

[CH14 | 11:23-12:20 | countdown_and_impact]

I tried to return in 1588. England was at war with Spain. The Armada. Queen Elizabeth forbade all ships from leaving port. April 22nd, 1588. I finally got two small ships. We sailed. May 6th. French pirates. Morocco. Twenty-four men died. All the supplies lost. We turned back. I tried again. 1589. Failed. 1590. Three years. August 15th, 1590. I finally returned. We saw smoke rising from the island. Then fire. We saw it again the next day. And the next. I thought, They're still there. They're alive. August 18th, 1590. Virginia's third birthday. I landed. The houses were gone. In their place: a tall wooden palisade. Like a fort. Curtain walls. Flankers. Inside, the ground was overgrown with grass. Scattered iron bars. Lead ingots. Rusted armor. Cannonballs. Their boats were gone. The small cannon, gone. On the right-hand post at the entrance, five feet up, carved in neat capital letters: CROATOAN. No cross. No distress mark. I also found my own chests. Broken open. My books torn apart. My maps soaked and ruined. My sketches destroyed. But no cross. That meant they left safely. They went to Croatoan. Manteo's island. They're there. They have to be there.

[CH15 | 12:20-13:16 | collapse_witnessing]

The captain said, We'll sail to Croatoan tomorrow. Find them. But that night, a storm hit. The anchor cable snapped. The ship was in danger. He had a choice. He said, We have 100 men on this ship. You're asking me to risk them all for 114 people who might not even be there. He chose to sail home. I begged him. Please. My daughter is there. My granddaughter is there. He said, We've done what we can. We tried. I couldn't argue with him. The storm was real. The risk was real. But I also couldn't look at that island anymore. Somewhere—inland, or on Croatoan—my daughter was waiting for me. Hoping I'd come back. And I was leaving her again. We sailed away. I never returned.

[CH16 | 13:16-14:00 | closure_reflection]

1593. I wrote to Richard Hakluyt from Ireland. I said I could only commit the colonists to the merciful providence of the Almighty. That's the last record of me. It's one thing to read that CROATOAN is a mystery. But it's another thing to stand in front of that post and know Eleanor and Ananias carved it. Know they stood there with chisels, carving the name of the place they were going, hoping you'd understand. They weren't lost. They knew where they were going. I was the one who couldn't reach them.
